FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A01
Guide signs identify the current road or help a driver reach a destination. The handbook includes route, information, destination, distance and location signs in this group. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A01
Guide signs are often rectangular but may have another shape. A companion arrow or destination word can show how to reach a road or facility. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A01
Numbers on route or exit guide signs identify a particular highway, interstate or exit rather than a speed requirement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A01
A junction guide can announce where named roads cross or meet the road being traveled. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A01
Milepost markers occur at mile intervals beside the road. The handbook describes numbering from zero at the southern or western state boundary where the route begins. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A01
The slow-moving-vehicle emblem identifies a vehicle traveling below 25 miles per hour under the handbook's definition. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A01
A designated-bicycle-route guide identifies a road used as an official bicycle route and calls for caution around riders. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A01
A public-parking guide points toward the available parking area. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A01
At a railroad crossbuck, slow, look and listen and yield to an approaching train. A panel beneath the crossbuck identifies the number of tracks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A01
A flashing red warning at a railroad crossing requires a complete stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A02
Construction and maintenance warning signs use orange backgrounds with black markings to announce dangers early enough for a speed adjustment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=34]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A02
Blue-and-white service signs direct travelers to facilities such as fuel, food, lodging, a hospital or camping. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=34]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A02
An express lane offers the option of paying a toll for an alternative to congested regular lanes; the source describes charges taken from a registered account. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=34]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A02
A reversible express lane changes direction during the day. The source says signs display a closed condition while the travel direction is being changed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=34]

Misconceptions: An exit or route number is not a speed limit; a service sign guides toward a facility rather than overriding a traffic restriction.
Mnemonic: Warn of the condition, guide to the destination, obey the closure.
Glossary: A guide supplies route information; a service sign points to a facility; a crossbuck identifies a rail crossing.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Toll eligibility, exemptions, operating hours, network descriptions and sign-asset rights remain verification debt.
